rules.statement: An absent attribute equals no value, not another absent one and not the empty string; exists is false for it.
guards: model:ConditionEvaluationTest#exists sees present values, empty ones included

rules.statement: A condition over a cost bound (nodes, depth, in values, CIDR blocks, literal length, total weight) does not compile.
properties: model:ConditionPropertyTest#A4 evaluation visits at most the node limit

rules.statement: Evaluation is two-valued: not negates its operand, so not over a comparison with an absent attribute is true.
properties: model:ConditionPropertyTest#A3 normalizing does not change decisions
guards: model:ConditionEvaluationTest#absent makes every comparison false and not negates it

rules.statement: Attributes are typed statically: a path outside the catalog, an operand of the wrong type, or a string literal for a Bool does not compile.

No attribute reference may read a credential header: `http.header.authorization`, `proxy-authorization`, `cookie`, `set-cookie`, `x-api-key`, `cosec-identity`, or the header the host reads API keys from (`cosec.pipeline.api-key-header`, RC1-21), whether in a condition or a rate limit rule's `key`. Every compiler of the host is given that header, and the pipeline never reads it for a condition either. A header name is an ASCII token (RFC 9110 tchar), matched case-insensitively with the ASCII fold on both the document and the request side, so no Unicode case mapping can reach a credential header; any other name does not compile. `ConditionChecker.attribute` refuses both, so every reference is checked in one place. A document with such a reference does not compile, through the control plane and cosec-migrate alike.
guards: model:ConditionCheckerTest#no attribute reference resolves a credential header
model:AttributeTest#a header name that is not an ASCII token does not parse
runtime:HttpAttributesTest#header names fold ASCII letters only
model:ConditionCheckerTest#a renamed api key header is a credential header
